name: ColdPlasma
description: Cold plasma model: electron-fluid current coupled with Maxwell's equations via a cold-plasma Ohm's law.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Cold-plasma current:

1n₀ ∂𝐣∂t = 1ε 𝐄 + 1ε n₀ 𝐣 × 𝐁₀

Faraday's law:

∂𝐁∂t + ∇ × 𝐄 = 0

Ampère's law:

-∂𝐄∂t + ∇ × 𝐁 = α²ε 𝐣

where (n₀, 𝐁₀) denotes an inhomogeneous background.
longDescriptionHtml:
This is a fluid electromagnetic model for a cold plasma response. The

electron fluid is represented only through its current, so thermal pressure and kinetic velocity-space effects are omitted. It is useful as a reduced model between vacuum Maxwell and fully kinetic Vlasov-Maxwell dynamics.

name: HasegawaWakatani
description: Hasegawa-Wakatani equations in 2D for drift-wave turbulence.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Density equation:

∂n∂t = C (φ - n) - [φ, n] - κ   ∂y φ + ν   ∇²ᴺ n

Vorticity equation:

∂ω∂t = C (φ - n) - [φ, ω] + ν   ∇²ᴺ ω

Potential equation:

Δ φ = ω

where [φ, n] = ∂ₓ φ ∂y n - ∂y φ ∂ₓ n, C = C(x, y) and κ and ν are constants (at the moment only N=1 is available).
longDescriptionHtml:
This is a reduced 2D drift-wave turbulence model. The electrostatic

potential is recovered from the vorticity at each step, and the coupled density-vorticity dynamics capture resistive drift-wave behavior without resolving full kinetic physics.

name: IncompressibleNavierStokesSPH
description: Incompressible Navier-Stokes equations discretized with smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH).
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Incompressible Navier-Stokes:

ρ (∂ₜ 𝐮 + 𝐮 · ∇ 𝐮) = -∇ p - ∇ · σ
∇ · 𝐮 = 0 .

where σ is the viscous stress tensor.

The viscous stress tensor for a Newtonian fluid is given by:

σ = -μ ( ∇ 𝐮 + (∇ 𝐮)ᵀ - 23 (∇ · 𝐮) 𝐈 )

where μ is the dynamic (shear) viscosity and 𝐈 is the identity tensor.
longDescriptionHtml: IncompressibleNavierStokesSPH is the particle-based SPH fluid model...

name: LinearExtendedMHDuniform
description: Linear extended MHD with zero-flow equilibrium, for uniform background conditions only.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Continuity:

∂ρ̃∂t + ∇ · (ρ₀ Ũ) = 0

Momentum:

ρ₀ ∂Ũ∂t + ∇ p̃ = (∇ × B̃) × 𝐁₀

Pressure:

∂p̃∂t + 53 p₀ ∇ · Ũ = 0

Induction:

∂B̃∂t - ∇ × ( Ũ × 𝐁₀ - 1ε ∇ × B̃ρ₀ × 𝐁₀ ) = 0
longDescriptionHtml:
LinearExtendedMHDuniform extends the linear MHD model with Hall

dynamics for a uniform equilibrium. It is targeted at wave propagation and mode studies where the equilibrium is simple but finite Hall corrections are important.

name: LinearMHD
description: Linear ideal MHD with zero-flow equilibrium for magnetohydrodynamic wave propagation.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Continuity (mass conservation):

∂ρ̃∂t + ∇ · (ρ₀ Ũ) = 0

Momentum (Lorentz force):

ρ₀ ∂Ũ∂t + ∇ p̃ = (∇ × B̃) × 𝐁₀ + (∇ × 𝐁₀) × B̃

Energy (adiabatic process):

∂p̃∂t + ∇ · (p₀ Ũ) + 23 p₀ ∇ · Ũ = 0

Induction (Faraday's law):

∂B̃∂t - ∇ × (Ũ × 𝐁₀) = 0.
longDescriptionHtml:
This model simulates small-amplitude perturbations in a magnetized plasma with a static

equilibrium magnetic field 𝐁₀ and zero background flow. The model solves the linearized ideal magnetohydrodynamic equations, which couple fluid dynamics (density, velocity, pressure) with magnetic field evolution.

The linear MHD system supports three wave families:

  • Alfvén waves: incompressible shear waves propagating along 𝐁₀
  • Fast magnetosonic waves: compressible waves with phase velocity above the Alfvén speed
  • Slow magnetosonic waves: compressible waves with phase velocity below the Alfvén speed

All evolved quantities are perturbations around a stationary equilibrium:

  • ρ̃ - density perturbation
  • Ũ - velocity perturbation
  • p̃ - pressure perturbation
  • B̃ - magnetic field perturbation

The corresponding equilibrium quantities are:

  • ρ₀ - background density
  • p₀ - background pressure
  • 𝐁₀ - background magnetic field

name: Poisson
description: Weak discretization of Poisson's equation with a diffusion matrix, stabilization and an optional time-dependent right-hand side.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Find φ ∈ H¹ such that

-∇ · D₀(𝐱) ∇ φ + n₀(𝐱) φ = ρ(t, 𝐱)

where n₀, ρ(t) : Ω → ℝ are real-valued functions, ρ(t) is parametrized by time t, and D₀ : Ω → ℝ3 × 3 is a positive matrix. Boundary terms from integration by parts are assumed to vanish.
longDescriptionHtml:
Poisson is the standalone elliptic field-solve model used for weak

diffusion/Poisson problems. It is also the building block reused by other models for initial electrostatic solves.

name: PressureLessSPH
description: Particle discretization of pressureless Euler flow with external forcing.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Continuity:

∂ₜ ρ + ∇ · (ρ 𝐮) = 0

Momentum:

∂ₜ (ρ 𝐮) + ∇ · (ρ 𝐮 ⊗ 𝐮) = 𝐅

where 𝐅 is an external force.
longDescriptionHtml:
PressureLessSPH is a meshfree particle model for a pressureless fluid.

It is primarily useful as a simple SPH benchmark or as a reduced particle transport model in a prescribed force field or potential.

name: ShearAlfven
description: Shear-Alfvén part of LinearMHD with zero-flow equilibrium.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Momentum:

ρ₀ ∂Ũ∂t = (∇ × B̃) × 𝐁₀

Induction:

∂B̃∂t - ∇ × (Ũ × 𝐁₀) = 0
longDescriptionHtml:
ShearAlfven is the incompressible magnetic-tension subsystem extracted

from linear MHD. It is useful when one wants to isolate Alfvénic propagation from the full linear MHD model.

name: TwoFluidQuasiNeutralToy
description: Linearized, quasi-neutral two-fluid model with zero electron inertia.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Ion momentum:

∂𝐮∂t = -∇ φ + 𝐮 × 𝐁₀ε + ν Δ 𝐮 + 𝐟

Electron momentum:

0 = ∇ φ - 𝐮ₑ × 𝐁₀ε + νₑ Δ 𝐮ₑ + 𝐟ₑ

Quasi-neutrality constraint:

∇ · (𝐮 - 𝐮ₑ) = 0

where 𝐁₀ is a static magnetic field and 𝐟, 𝐟ₑ are given forcing terms.
longDescriptionHtml:
TwoFluidQuasiNeutralToy is a reduced linear two-fluid benchmark with

zero electron inertia. It is meant for studying the quasi-neutral solve and the coupled ion/electron velocity response in a simplified setting.

References

[1] Juan Vicente Gutiérrez-Santacreu, Omar Maj, Marco Restelli: Finite element discretization of a Stokes-like model arising in plasma physics, Journal of Computational Physics 2018.

name: VariationalBarotropicFluid
description: Barotropic fluid equations discretized with a variational method.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Continuity:

∂ₜ ρ + ∇ · (ρ 𝐮) = 0

Momentum:

∂ₜ (ρ 𝐮) + ∇ · (ρ 𝐮 ⊗ 𝐮) + ρ ∇ (ρ 𝒰(ρ))∂ ρ = 0

where the internal energy per unit mass is 𝒰(ρ) = ρ/2.
longDescriptionHtml:
This is the simplest variational compressible-fluid model in Struphy.

It keeps only density and velocity and uses a barotropic closure rather than a separate entropy or pressure evolution equation.

name: VariationalCompressibleFluid
description: Fully compressible fluid equations discretized with a variational method.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Continuity:

∂ₜ ρ + ∇ · (ρ 𝐮) = 0

Momentum:

∂ₜ (ρ 𝐮) + ∇ · (ρ 𝐮 ⊗ 𝐮) + ρ ∇ (ρ 𝒰(ρ, s))∂ ρ + s ∇ (ρ 𝒰(ρ, s))∂ s = 0

Entropy:

∂ₜ s + ∇ · (s 𝐮) = 0

where the internal energy per unit mass is 𝒰(ρ) = ργ-1 \exp(s / ρ).
longDescriptionHtml:
VariationalCompressibleFluid is the entropy-based compressible fluid

model in the variational family. It is the natural non-magnetic counterpart to the full variational MHD models.

name: VariationalPressurelessFluid
description: Pressure-less fluid equations discretized with a variational method.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Continuity:

∂ₜ ρ + ∇ · (ρ 𝐮) = 0

Momentum:

∂ₜ (ρ 𝐮) + ∇ · (ρ 𝐮 ⊗ 𝐮) = 0
longDescriptionHtml:
This is the pressureless limit of the variational fluid hierarchy. It

is intended as a reduced benchmark and as a simple transport model with conservative density and momentum updates.

name: ViscoResistiveDeltafMHD
description: Delta-f visco-resistive MHD equations discretized with a variational method.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Continuity:

∂ₜ ρ̃ + ∇ · ( (ρ̃ + ρ₀) ũ ) = 0

Momentum:

∂ₜ ( (ρ̃ + ρ₀) ũ ) + ∇ · ( (ρ̃ + ρ₀) ũ ⊗ ũ ) + 1γ - 1 ∇ p̃ + 𝐁₀ × ∇ × B̃ + B̃ × ∇ × 𝐁₀ + B̃ × ∇ × B̃ - ∇ · ( (μ + μₐ(𝐱)) ∇ ũ ) = 0

Pressure:

∂ₜ p̃ + ũ · ∇ (p̃ + p₀) + γ (p̃ + p₀) ∇ · ũ = 1γ - 1 ( (μ + μₐ(𝐱)) |∇ ũ|² + (η + ηₐ(𝐱)) |∇ × B̃|² )

Induction:

∂ₜ B̃ + ∇ × ( (B̃ + 𝐁₀) × ũ ) + ∇ × (η + ηₐ(𝐱)) ∇ × B̃ = 0

Here μₐ(𝐱) and ηₐ(𝐱) are artificial viscosity and resistivity coefficients.
longDescriptionHtml:
ViscoResistiveDeltafMHD is the dissipative perturbative MHD model using

pressure as thermodynamic variable. It is intended for departures from a background equilibrium that are not strictly linear but still naturally formulated as perturbations.

name: ViscoResistiveDeltafMHD_with_q
description: Delta-f visco-resistive MHD equations, with the q variable (square root of the pressure), discretized with a variational method.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Continuity:

∂ₜ ρ̃ + ∇ · (ρ₀ ũ) = 0

Momentum:

∂ₜ (ρ₀ ũ) + 2 q₀γ - 1 ∇ q̃ + 2 q̃γ - 1 ∇ q₀ + 2 q̃γ - 1 ∇ q̃ + 𝐁₀ × ∇ × B̃ + B̃ × ∇ × 𝐁₀ - ∇ · ( (μ + μₐ(𝐱)) ∇ ũ ) = 0

Energy-like variable:

∂ₜ q̃ + ∇ · ( (q₀ + q̃) ũ ) + ( γ2 - 1 ) (q₀ + q̃) ∇ · ũ = 0

Induction:

∂ₜ B̃ + ∇ × ( (𝐁₀ + B̃) × ũ ) + ∇ × (η + ηₐ(𝐱)) ∇ × B̃ = 0

Here μₐ(𝐱) and ηₐ(𝐱) are artificial viscosity and resistivity coefficients.
longDescriptionHtml:
This model is the delta f dissipative MHD formulation in the

q-variable representation. It is aimed at perturbative nonlinear MHD studies where the q-formulation is preferred numerically.

name: ViscoResistiveLinearMHD
description: Linear visco-resistive MHD equations discretized with a variational method.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Continuity:

∂ₜ ρ̃ + ∇ · (ρ₀ ũ) = 0

Momentum:

∂ₜ (ρ₀ ũ) + 1γ - 1 ∇ p̃ + 𝐁₀ × ∇ × B̃ + B̃ × ∇ × 𝐁₀ - ∇ · ( (μ + μₐ(𝐱)) ∇ ũ ) = 0

Pressure:

∂ₜ p̃ + ũ · ∇ p₀ + γ p₀ ∇ · ũ = 1γ - 1 ( (μ + μₐ(𝐱)) |∇ ũ|² + (η + ηₐ(𝐱)) |∇ × B̃|² )

Induction:

∂ₜ B̃ + ∇ × (𝐁₀ × ũ) + ∇ × (η + ηₐ(𝐱)) ∇ × B̃ = 0

Here μₐ(𝐱) and ηₐ(𝐱) are artificial viscosity and resistivity coefficients.
longDescriptionHtml:
This is the linear dissipative MHD model with pressure as primitive

thermodynamic variable. It is intended for small-amplitude perturbations around an equilibrium while retaining explicit viscosity and resistivity.

name: ViscoResistiveLinearMHD_with_q
description: Linear visco-resistive MHD equations, with the q variable (square root of the pressure), discretized with a variational method.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Continuity:

∂ₜ ρ̃ + ∇ · (ρ₀ ũ) = 0

Momentum:

∂ₜ (ρ₀ ũ) + 2 q₀γ - 1 ∇ q̃ + 2 q̃γ - 1 ∇ q₀ + 𝐁₀ × ∇ × B̃ + B̃ × ∇ × 𝐁₀ - ∇ · ( (μ + μₐ(𝐱)) ∇ ũ ) = 0

Energy-like variable:

∂ₜ q̃ + ∇ q₀ · ũ + ( γ2 - 1 ) q₀ ∇ · ũ = 0

Induction:

∂ₜ B̃ + ∇ × (𝐁₀ × ũ) + ∇ × (η + ηₐ(𝐱)) ∇ × B̃ = 0

Here μₐ(𝐱) and ηₐ(𝐱) are artificial viscosity and resistivity coefficients.
longDescriptionHtml:
This variant of the linear dissipative MHD model uses the square root

of the pressure as primary thermodynamic variable, which is convenient for the corresponding variational discretization.

name: ViscoResistiveMHD
description: Full (non-linear) visco-resistive MHD equations discretized with a variational method.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Continuity:

∂ₜ ρ + ∇ · (ρ 𝐮) = 0

Momentum:

∂ₜ (ρ 𝐮) + ∇ · (ρ 𝐮 ⊗ 𝐮) + ρ ∇ (ρ 𝒰(ρ, s))∂ ρ + s ∇ (ρ 𝒰(ρ, s))∂ s + 𝐁 × ∇ × 𝐁 - ∇ · ( (μ + μₐ(𝐱)) ∇ 𝐮 ) = 0

Entropy:

∂ₜ s + ∇ · (s 𝐮) = 1T ( (μ + μₐ(𝐱)) |∇ 𝐮|² + (η + ηₐ(𝐱)) |∇ × 𝐁|² )

Induction:

∂ₜ 𝐁 + ∇ × (𝐁 × 𝐮) + ∇ × (η + ηₐ(𝐱)) ∇ × 𝐁 = 0

where the internal energy per unit mass is 𝒰(ρ) = ργ-1 \exp(s / ρ), and μₐ(𝐱) and ηₐ(𝐱) are artificial viscosity and resistivity coefficients.
longDescriptionHtml:
ViscoResistiveMHD is the full nonlinear dissipative MHD model in the

entropy formulation. It is the most complete variational MHD model in this family when both viscosity and resistivity are required.

name: ViscoResistiveMHD_with_p
description: Full (non-linear) visco-resistive MHD equations, with the pressure variable, discretized with a variational method.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Continuity:

∂ₜ ρ + ∇ · (ρ 𝐮) = 0

Momentum:

∂ₜ (ρ 𝐮) + ∇ · (ρ 𝐮 ⊗ 𝐮) + 1γ - 1 ∇ p + 𝐁 × ∇ × 𝐁 - ∇ · ( (μ + μₐ(𝐱)) ∇ 𝐮 ) = 0

Pressure:

∂ₜ p + u · ∇ p + γ p ∇ · u = 1γ - 1 ( (μ + μₐ(𝐱)) |∇ 𝐮|² + (η + ηₐ(𝐱)) |∇ × 𝐁|² )

Induction:

∂ₜ 𝐁 + ∇ × (𝐁 × 𝐮) + ∇ × (η + ηₐ(𝐱)) ∇ × 𝐁 = 0

Here μₐ(𝐱) and ηₐ(𝐱) are artificial viscosity and resistivity coefficients.
longDescriptionHtml:
This is the pressure-based full nonlinear dissipative MHD model. It is

the natural counterpart to the entropy- and q-based full MHD variants when pressure is preferred as primitive thermodynamic variable.

name: ViscoResistiveMHD_with_q
description: Full (non-linear) visco-resistive MHD equations, with the q variable (square root of the pressure), discretized with a variational method.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Continuity:

∂ₜ ρ + ∇ · (ρ 𝐮) = 0

Momentum:

∂ₜ (ρ 𝐮) + ∇ · (ρ 𝐮 ⊗ 𝐮) + 2 qγ - 1 ∇ q + 𝐁 × ∇ × 𝐁 - ∇ · ( (μ + μₐ(𝐱)) ∇ 𝐮 ) = 0

Energy-like variable:

∂ₜ q + ∇ · (q 𝐮) + ( γ2 - 1 ) q ∇ · 𝐮 = 2 qγ - 1 ( (μ + μₐ(𝐱)) |∇ 𝐮|² + (η + ηₐ(𝐱)) |∇ × 𝐁|² )

Induction:

∂ₜ 𝐁 + ∇ × (𝐁 × 𝐮) + ∇ × (η + ηₐ(𝐱)) ∇ × 𝐁 = 0

Here μₐ(𝐱) and ηₐ(𝐱) are artificial viscosity and resistivity coefficients.
longDescriptionHtml:
This model is the full nonlinear q-based dissipative MHD formulation.

It is useful when the square-root pressure variable is preferred in the variational discretization while still retaining full nonlinear magnetic dynamics.

name: ViscousEulerSPH
description: Euler equations with viscosity discretized with smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH).
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Continuity:

∂ₜ ρ + ∇ · (ρ 𝐮) = 0

Momentum:

ρ (∂ₜ 𝐮 + 𝐮 · ∇ 𝐮) = -∇ ( ρ² ∂𝒰(ρ, S)∂ρ ) - ∇ · π

Entropy:

∂ₜ S + 𝐮 · ∇ S = 0

where S denotes the entropy per unit mass and π is the viscous stress tensor.

The viscous stress tensor for a Newtonian fluid is given by:

σ = -μ ( ∇ 𝐮 + (∇ 𝐮)ᵀ - 23 (∇ · 𝐮) 𝐈 )

where μ is the dynamic (shear) viscosity and 𝐈 is the identity tensor.

The internal energy per unit mass can be defined in two ways:

isothermal:    𝒰(ρ, S) = κ(S) \log ρ

polytropic:    𝒰(ρ, S) = κ(S) ργ - 1γ - 1
longDescriptionHtml:
ViscousEulerSPH is the particle-based SPH fluid model with optional

pressure and viscosity contributions. It is intended for meshfree fluid experiments rather than FEEC-based field simulations.

name: ViscousFluid
description: Full (non-linear) viscous Navier-Stokes equations discretized with a variational method.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Continuity:

∂ₜ ρ + ∇ · (ρ 𝐮) = 0

Momentum:

∂ₜ (ρ 𝐮) + ∇ · (ρ 𝐮 ⊗ 𝐮) + ρ ∇ (ρ 𝒰(ρ, s))∂ ρ + s ∇ (ρ 𝒰(ρ, s))∂ s - ∇ · ( (μ + μₐ(𝐱)) ∇ 𝐮 ) = 0

Entropy:

∂ₜ s + ∇ · (s 𝐮) = 1T ( (μ + μₐ(𝐱)) |∇ 𝐮|² )

where the internal energy per unit mass is 𝒰(ρ) = ργ-1 \exp(s / ρ). and μₐ(𝐱) is an artificial viscosity coefficient.
longDescriptionHtml:
ViscousFluid is the non-magnetic viscous member of the variational

fluid family. It is suited for compressible hydrodynamics with entropy transport and viscous heating but without magnetic effects.

name: DeterministicParticleDiffusion
description: Diffusion equation discretized with a deterministic particle method.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Find u : ℝ × Ω → ℝ⁺ such that

∂u∂t + ∇ · ( 𝐅(u) u ) = 0,    𝐅(u) = -𝔻 ∇ uu

where 𝔻 : Ω → ℝ3 × 3 is a positive diffusion matrix. At the moment only matrices of the form D * Id are implemented, where D > 0 is a positive diffusion coefficient.
longDescriptionHtml:
This is a particle discretization of diffusion where particles follow a

deterministic drift derived from the current estimate of the density. It is intended mainly for diffusion-method development and verification rather than plasma dynamics.

name: DriftKineticElectrostaticAdiabatic
description: Electrostatic drift-kinetic model for a single ion species with adiabatic electrons.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Drift-kinetic equation:

∂f∂t + [ v∥ 𝐁*B*∥ + 𝐄* × 𝐛₀B*∥ ] · ∂f∂𝐗 + [ 1ε 𝐁*B*∥ · 𝐄* ] · ∂f∂v∥ = 0

Poisson equation:

-∇⟂ · ( n₀|B₀|² ∇⟂ φ ) + 1ε n₀ ( 1 + 1Z ε 1T₀ φ ) = 1ε ∫ f B*∥   d v∥ d μ

where f(𝐗, v∥, μ, t) is the guiding center distribution and

𝐄* = -∇ φ - ε μ ∇ |B₀|,    𝐁* = 𝐁₀ + ε v∥ ∇ × 𝐛₀,    B*∥ = 𝐁* · 𝐛₀

The control variate method can be activated in the Poisson equation; if enabled, the following Poisson equation is solved:

-∇⟂ · ( n₀|B₀|² ∇⟂ φ ) + 1Z ε² n₀T₀ φ = 1ε ∫ (f - f₀) B*∥   d v∥ d μ
longDescriptionHtml:
This model is an electrostatic drift-kinetic reduction for strongly

magnetized ions in a fixed magnetic equilibrium. Electrons are not evolved kinetically; instead they enter through the adiabatic response in the quasi-neutrality solve. The implementation supports control variates for the field solve.

name: GuidingCenter
description: Guiding-center equation for a single species in a static background magnetic field.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Guiding-center Vlasov equation:

∂f∂t + [ v∥ 𝐁*B*∥ + 𝐄* × 𝐛₀B*∥ ] · ∂f∂𝐗 + [ 1ε 𝐁*B*∥ · 𝐄* ] · ∂f∂v∥ = 0

where f(𝐗, v∥, μ, t) is the guiding center distribution and

𝐄* = -ε μ ∇ |B₀|,    𝐁* = 𝐁₀ + ε v∥ ∇ × 𝐛₀,    B*∥ = 𝐁* · 𝐛₀
longDescriptionHtml:
GuidingCenter is the reduced kinetic model used when fast gyromotion is

averaged out and only guiding-center motion needs to be resolved. It evolves particles in a fixed magnetic background without any self-consistent field solve.

name: LinearVlasovAmpereOneSpecies
description: Linearized Vlasov-Ampère equations for one kinetic species around a Maxwellian background.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Linearized Ampère's law:

∂Ẽ∂t = -α²ε ∫ℝ³ 𝐯 f̃   d³ 𝐯

Linearized Vlasov equation:

∂f̃∂t + 𝐯 · ∇ f̃ + 1ε ( 𝐄₀ + 𝐯 × 𝐁₀ ) · ∂f̃∂𝐯 = 1vₜₕ² ε Ẽ · 𝐯 f₀

where Z=-1 and A=1/1836 for electrons. The background distribution function f₀ is a uniform Maxwellian

f₀ = n₀(𝐱)( √(2 π) vₜₕ )³ \exp ( - |𝐯|²2 vₜₕ² )

and the background electric field has to verify the following compatibility condition between with background density

∇𝐱 \ln (n₀(𝐱)) = 1vₜₕ² ε 𝐄₀

At initial time the weak Poisson equation is solved once to weakly satisfy Gauss' law,

∫Ω ∇ ψᵀ · ∇ φ   d 𝐱
=α²ε ∫Ω ∫ℝ³ ψ   f̃   d³ 𝐯   d 𝐱
∀ ψ ∈ H¹
Ẽ(t=0)=-∇ φ(t=0)

Moreover, it is assumed that

∫ℝ³ 𝐯 f₀   d³ 𝐯 = 0
longDescriptionHtml:
LinearVlasovAmpereOneSpecies is the linearized delta-f counterpart of

VlasovAmpereOneSpecies. It is intended for weakly perturbed kinetic problems around a prescribed Maxwellian equilibrium and is especially useful for linear instability or damping studies.

name: RandomParticleDiffusion
description: Diffusion equation discretized with a random particle method, via a Wiener process.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Find u : ℝ × Ω → ℝ⁺ such that

∂u∂t - D   Δ u = 0

where D > 0 is a positive diffusion coefficient.
longDescriptionHtml:
This model is the stochastic counterpart of the deterministic particle

diffusion model. It is intended for diffusion-method development and comparisons between random-walk and deterministic transport strategies.

name: Vlasov
description: Vlasov equation for a single species in a static background magnetic field.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Vlasov equation:

∂f∂t + 𝐯 · ∇ f + ( 𝐯 × 𝐁₀ ) · ∂f∂𝐯 = 0
longDescriptionHtml:
Vlasov is the simplest kinetic test-particle model in the 6D hierarchy.

It evolves particles in a static magnetic background without electric or magnetic self-consistency.

name: VlasovAmpereOneSpecies
description: Vlasov-Ampère system for a single kinetic species in an electric field.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Vlasov equation:

∂f∂t + 𝐯 · ∇ f + 1ε ( 𝐄 + 𝐯 × 𝐁₀ ) · ∂f∂𝐯 = 0

Ampère's law:

-∂𝐄∂t = α²ε ∫ℝ³ 𝐯 f   d³ 𝐯

Initial Poisson equation: At t=0, solve weakly for the electric potential φ:

∫Ω ∇ ψᵀ · ∇ φ   d 𝐱=α²ε ∫Ω ∫ℝ³ ψ   (f - f₀)   d³ 𝐯   d 𝐱    ∀ ψ ∈ H¹
𝐄(t=0)=-∇ φ(t=0)
longDescriptionHtml:
This model couples the kinetic Vlasov equation for the particle distribution function

with Ampère's law for the electric field evolution. It includes the effect of a static background magnetic field 𝐁₀ and solves the initial Poisson equation to satisfy Gauss's law at t=0. The model uses a particle-in-cell (PIC) method with finite element exterior calculus (FEEC) for the electromagnetic fields.

All field variables are perturbations around a reference equilibrium distribution. The model enables studies of kinetic instabilities, particle-wave interactions, and nonlinear plasma physics without assuming a fluid approximation.

name: VlasovMaxwellOneSpecies
description: Vlasov-Maxwell equations for one kinetic species.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Vlasov equation:

∂f∂t + 𝐯 · ∇ f + 1ε ( 𝐄 + 𝐯 × ( 𝐁 + 𝐁₀ ) ) · ∂f∂𝐯 = 0

Ampère's law:

-∂𝐄∂t + ∇ × 𝐁 = α²ε ∫ℝ³ 𝐯 f   d³ 𝐯

Faraday's law:

∂𝐁∂t + ∇ × 𝐄 = 0

where Z=-1 and A=1/1836 for electrons.

At initial time the weak Poisson equation is solved once to weakly satisfy Gauss' law,

∫Ω ∇ ψᵀ · ∇ φ   d 𝐱=α²ε ∫Ω ∫ℝ³ ψ   (f - f₀)   d³ 𝐯   d 𝐱    ∀ ψ ∈ H¹
𝐄(t=0)=-∇ φ(t=0)

Moreover, it is assumed that

∇ × 𝐁₀ = α²ε ∫ℝ³ 𝐯 f₀   d³ 𝐯

where 𝐁₀ is the static equilibrium magnetic field.
longDescriptionHtml:
VlasovMaxwellOneSpecies is the fully electromagnetic one-species PIC

model in Struphy. It evolves particles and fields self-consistently and supports an optional control-variate formulation for the field coupling.

name: LinearVlasovMaxwellOneSpecies
description: Linearized Vlasov-Maxwell equations for one kinetic species around a Maxwellian background.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Linearized Ampère's law:

∂Ẽ∂t = ∇ × B̃ - α²ε ∫ℝ³ 𝐯 f̃   d³ 𝐯

Linearized Faraday's law:

∂B̃∂t = -∇ × Ẽ

Linearized Vlasov equation:

∂f̃∂t + 𝐯 · ∇ f̃ + 1ε ( 𝐄₀ + 𝐯 × 𝐁₀ ) · ∂f̃∂𝐯 = 1vₜₕ² ε Ẽ · 𝐯 f₀

where Z=-1 and A=1/1836 for electrons. The background distribution function f₀ is a uniform Maxwellian

f₀ = n₀(𝐱)( √(2 π) vₜₕ )³ \exp ( - |𝐯|²2 vₜₕ² )

and the background electric field has to verify the following compatibility condition between with background density

∇𝐱 \ln (n₀(𝐱)) = 1vₜₕ² ε 𝐄₀

At initial time the weak Poisson equation is solved once to weakly satisfy Gauss' law,

∫Ω ∇ ψᵀ · ∇ φ   d 𝐱
=α²ε ∫Ω ∫ℝ³ ψ   f̃   d³ 𝐯   d 𝐱
∀ ψ ∈ H¹
Ẽ(t=0)=-∇ φ(t=0)

Moreover, it is assumed that

∫ℝ³ 𝐯 f₀   d³ 𝐯 = 0
longDescriptionHtml:
LinearVlasovMaxwellOneSpecies is the electromagnetic extension of the

linear delta-f Vlasov model. It is intended for weakly perturbed kinetic electromagnetic waves and instabilities around a prescribed equilibrium.

name: ColdPlasmaVlasov
description: Hybrid cold-plasma model: a cold electron fluid coupled with a hot kinetic species and Maxwell's equations.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Hot Vlasov species:

∂f∂t + 𝐯 · ∇ f + 1εₕ \Big[ 𝐄 + 𝐯 × ( 𝐁 + 𝐁₀ ) \Big] · ∂f∂𝐯 = 0

Cold-plasma current:

1n₀ ∂𝐣c∂t = 1εc 𝐄 + 1εc n₀ 𝐣c × 𝐁₀

Faraday's law:

∂𝐁∂t + ∇ × 𝐄 = 0

Ampère's law:

-∂𝐄∂t + ∇ × 𝐁 = α²εₕ ( 𝐣c + ∫ℝ³ 𝐯 f   d³ 𝐯 )

where (n₀, 𝐁₀) denotes an inhomogeneous background.

At initial time the Poisson equation is solved once to weakly satisfy the Gauss law:

∇ · 𝐄 = ν α²εₕ ∫ℝ³ f   d³ 𝐯
longDescriptionHtml:
ColdPlasmaVlasov is an electromagnetic hybrid model that keeps a cold

fluid response for the thermal electrons and a kinetic PIC description for a hot species. It is designed for problems where the energetic population matters kinetically but the bulk response can still be treated as cold.

name: LinearMHDDriftkineticCC
description: Hybrid linear ideal MHD coupled with energetic ions (5D drift-kinetic) via the current-coupling scheme.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

MHD continuity:

∂ρ̃∂t + ∇ · (ρ₀ Ũ) = 0

MHD momentum:

ρ₀ ∂Ũ∂t + ∇ p̃ = (∇ × B̃) × 𝐁 + (∇ × 𝐁₀) × B̃ + AₕAb [ 1ε ngc Ũ - 1ε 𝐉gc - ∇ × 𝐌gc ] × 𝐁

MHD pressure:

∂p̃∂t + ∇ · (p₀ Ũ) + 23 p₀ ∇ · Ũ = 0

MHD induction:

∂B̃∂t - ∇ × (Ũ × 𝐁) = 0

Energetic-particle drift-kinetic equation:

∂fₕ∂t + 1B∥* ( v∥ 𝐁* - 𝐛₀ × 𝐄* ) · ∇ fₕ + 1ε 1B∥* (𝐁* · 𝐄*) ∂fₕ∂v∥ = 0

Energetic-particle moments:

ngc = ∫ fₕ B∥*   d v∥ d μ

𝐉gc = ∫ fₕB∥* ( v∥ 𝐁* - 𝐛₀ × 𝐄* )   d v∥ d μ

𝐌gc = -∫ fₕ B∥* μ 𝐛₀   d v∥ d μ

where

B*∥ = 𝐛₀ · 𝐁*
𝐁*=𝐁 + ε v∥ ∇ × 𝐛₀
𝐄*=-Ũ × 𝐁 - ε μ ∇ (𝐛₀ · 𝐁)
longDescriptionHtml:
LinearMHDDriftkineticCC is the reduced-kinetic hybrid current-coupling

model for energetic ions. It is useful when gyrophase averaging is acceptable but energetic-particle feedback on linear MHD still has to be retained.

name: LinearMHDVlasovCC
description: Hybrid linear MHD coupled with energetic ions (6D Vlasov) via the current-coupling scheme.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

MHD continuity:

∂ρ̃∂t + ∇ · (ρ₀ Ũ) = 0

MHD momentum:

ρ₀ ∂Ũ∂t + ∇ p̃ = (∇ × B̃) × 𝐁₀ + 𝐉₀ × B̃ \color{blue} + AₕAb 1ε ( nₕ Ũ - nₕ 𝐮ₕ ) × (𝐁₀ + B̃) \color{black}

MHD pressure:

∂p̃∂t + (γ - 1) ∇ · (p₀ Ũ) + p₀ ∇ · Ũ = 0

MHD induction:

∂B̃∂t = ∇ × (Ũ × 𝐁₀),    ∇ · B̃ = 0

Energetic-particle Vlasov equation:

∂fₕ∂t + 𝐯 · ∇ fₕ + 1ε [ \color{blue} (𝐁₀ + B̃) × Ũ \color{black} + 𝐯 × (𝐁₀ + B̃) ] · ∂fₕ∂𝐯 = 0

Energetic-particle moments:

nₕ = ∫ℝ³ fₕ   d³ 𝐯,    nₕ 𝐮ₕ = ∫ℝ³ fₕ 𝐯   d³ 𝐯

where 𝐉₀ = ∇×𝐁₀.
longDescriptionHtml:
LinearMHDVlasovCC is a current-coupling hybrid model for small

perturbations around an MHD equilibrium. It is intended for energetic particle effects on linear MHD waves and instabilities without the cost of a fully kinetic background plasma.

name: LinearMHDVlasovPC
description: Hybrid linear MHD coupled with energetic ions (6D Vlasov) via the pressure-coupling scheme.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

MHD continuity:

∂ρ̃∂t + ∇ · (ρ₀ Ũ) = 0

MHD momentum:

ρ₀ ∂Ũ∂t + ∇ p̃ + AₕAb ∇ · ℙ̃h,⟂ = (∇ × B̃) × 𝐁₀ + 𝐉₀ × B̃

𝐉₀ = ∇ × 𝐁₀

MHD pressure:

∂p̃∂t + ∇ · (p₀ Ũ) + 23 p₀ ∇ · Ũ = 0

MHD induction:

∂B̃∂t - ∇ × (Ũ × 𝐁₀) = 0

Energetic-particle Vlasov equation:

∂fₕ∂t + (𝐯 + Ũ⟂) · ∇ fₕ + [ 1ε 𝐯 × (𝐁₀ + B̃) - ∇ Ũ⟂ · 𝐯 ] · ∂fₕ∂𝐯 = 0

Perpendicular pressure tensor:

ℙ̃h,⟂ = ∫ 𝐯⟂ 𝐯⟂ᵀ fₕ   d 𝐯
longDescriptionHtml:
LinearMHDVlasovPC is the pressure-coupling counterpart to the

current-coupling hybrid model. It is targeted at linear problems where energetic-particle pressure anisotropy is the relevant feedback channel on the bulk MHD dynamics.

name: Maxwell
description: Maxwell's equations in vacuum for electromagnetic field evolution.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Ampère's law (no current):

∂𝐄∂t - ∇ × 𝐁 = 0

Faraday's law:

∂𝐁∂t + ∇ × 𝐄 = 0
longDescriptionHtml:
This model simulates the propagation of electromagnetic waves in vacuum

using Maxwell's equations without sources. It uses a finite element exterior calculus (FEEC) formulation with the electric field in H(curl) and the magnetic field in H(div) spaces.

name: ToyDrift
description: Electrostatic drift toy model for a single ion species in a given background magnetic field.
pdeHtml:
PDEs solved by model:

Drift equation:

∂f∂t + 𝐄 × 𝐛₀B*∥ · ∂f∂𝐗 = 0

Poisson equation:

-∇ · ∇ φ = ∫ f B*∥   d v∥ d μ

where f(𝐗, v∥, μ, t) is the guiding center distribution and

𝐄 = -∇ φ,    𝐁* = 𝐁₀ + ε v∥ ∇ × 𝐛₀,    B*∥ = 𝐁* · 𝐛₀

The control variate method can be activated in the Poisson equation; if enabled, the following Poisson equation is solved:

-∇ · ∇ φ = ∫ (f - f₀) B*∥   d v∥ d μ
longDescriptionHtml:
ToyDrift is a stripped-down guiding-center model used to isolate the

electrostatic drift part of the dynamics. It is intended for algorithm prototyping and reduced verification problems rather than production drift-kinetic studies.
